title: PackLockfile
description: Reproducible-build lockfile pinning resolved versions of every pack a workspace depends on. This description is the v2 home of the lockfile resolution rules (re-homed from v1 `node-packs.md` §"Dependency resolution + lockfile" and §"Transitive dependency resolution" by RFC 0266). A workspace records its lockfile alongside its workflow definitions; on subsequent installs the registry resolver MUST honor the lockfile's exact versions rather than re-running semver resolution. This guarantees that a workflow that ran against `vendor.openwop.rust-hello@1.0.0` will still run against `1.0.0` even after `1.0.1` is published. When a lockfile is present a resolver MUST verify each entry's `integrity` (`pack_integrity_mismatch`) and, when recorded, its `signature` (`pack_signature_invalid`); MUST confirm the host advertises every entry's `peerDependencies` (`pack_peer_dependency_missing`); and MUST refuse a workspace that references a pack the lockfile does not list (`pack_lockfile_incomplete`). Integrity is verified per entry regardless of registry: there is no cross-registry trust transfer. A pinned version the registry no longer serves fails with `pack_version_not_found`. Resolution without a lockfile picks the highest version satisfying each range, recursing through each pack's `dependencies`; when two paths select different versions of one pack the resolver MUST search for a single version satisfying both ranges, and fails with `pack_dependency_conflict` when none does. Pack `dependencies` MUST form a DAG; re-entering a pack already on the active path fails with `pack_dependency_cycle`. Every resolved pack, direct and transitive, appears once in `packs[]`. Two resolvers run against the same registry snapshot, top-level manifests and overrides MUST produce byte-identical lockfiles: `packs[]` sorted by `name` then `version`, each `dependencies` map's keys sorted, canonical JSON.

lockfileVersion.description: Lockfile schema version. Bumped when the lockfile structure changes incompatibly. v1.0 ships at lockfileVersion 1.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp the lockfile was written. Used for audit + cache-bust diagnostics; resolvers MUST NOT use this for resolution decisions.

registry.description: Optional source-of-truth registry URL the resolved versions were fetched from (e.g., `https://packs.openwop.dev`). Multi-registry workspaces include this for audit. Single-registry workspaces MAY omit.

packs.description: Resolved pack records, one per pack referenced (transitively) by the workspace's workflow definitions. Order is informational only; resolvers MUST NOT rely on order. Empty arrays are allowed (a workspace with no packs).

overrides.description: Optional override map (override pinning). Keys are pack names; values are exact pinned versions that resolvers MUST honor ahead of normal range resolution. The override version MUST still satisfy at least one parent's declared range — silently breaking the contract fails with `pack_dependency_conflict`. Use sparingly: security patches, conflict resolution, supply-chain pinning.

additionalProperties.description: Exact pinned version that overrides this pack's normal range resolution.

fallbackRegistries.description: Optional ordered list of fallback registry base URLs (registry mirror and federation; re-homed from v1 `registry-operations.md` §"Registry mirror + federation" by RFC 0266). When a pack is not found in the primary `registry`, resolvers MUST consult each fallback in order. The first registry returning a 200 for the version manifest wins. Trust roots are per-registry — a fallback being listed here does NOT imply trust transitivity. Each pack's signature is verified against the issuing registry's `signingKeys[]` allow-list; listing a fallback does not trust every key it lists. A fallback that returns a transport-layer error (timeout, DNS, connection refused) is `pack_registry_unreachable` — the caller MAY retry on a different fallback or fail closed. A fetched pack whose signing key the issuing registry's `signingKeys[]` does not allow for the pack's namespace is `pack_namespace_unauthorized`.

name.description: Pack name per `node-pack-manifest.schema.json` `name`. Reverse-DNS-style; namespace prefix is one of the canonical tiers.

version.description: Resolved exact version (no ranges). Semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[-PRERELEASE][+BUILD]. The resolver MUST pin to this exact version on subsequent installs.

resolved.description: Optional canonical URL the tarball was fetched from. Audit aid; resolvers MUST verify the `integrity` field even if this URL is present.

integrity.description: Subresource-integrity-style hash of the tarball: literal `sha256-` followed by 43-char base64-encoded SHA-256 digest with trailing `=` padding. Resolvers MUST verify the downloaded tarball's SHA-256 matches before extraction. Hash mismatch MUST fail the install with `pack_integrity_mismatch`.

signature.description: Optional pack signature material (Ed25519). When present, resolvers MUST verify the signature against the publisher's advertised public key.

value.description: Base64-encoded Ed25519 signature over the tarball.

dependencies.description: Pinned versions for this pack's `dependencies` (per its manifest). Each key is a pack name; each value is the resolved exact version. Pinned recursively — a transitively-installed pack appears once in the top-level `packs[]` array AND as a value in each parent's `dependencies` map.

peerDependencies.description: Echo of this pack's manifest `peerDependencies` for audit. Resolvers MUST verify that the host's `/.well-known/openwop` advertises every key listed here (per host-capabilities.md §"Capability negotiation"). Lockfile records the host-capability values the workspace committed to at lockfile-write time; mismatches at install time MAY warn (host advertises richer set) but MUST fail if a peer-dep is missing.
